reference: The IEC 60364-5-52 correction-factor tables re-typed from published transcriptions of the standard (ambient air B.52.14, ground temperature B.52.15, soil thermal resistivity B.52.16, grouping B.52.17, buried grouping B.52.18, thermal insulation Table 52.2), the Annex G voltage-drop closed form u = b(rho1 L/S cos(phi) + lambda L sin(phi)) I_B, the IEC 60364-4-43 434.5.2 adiabatic equation with the Table 43A k values, the 433.1 I_B <= I_n <= I_z rule and the IEC 60364-5-54 Table 54.2 protective-conductor rule - all implemented independently in python. The raw current-carrying-capacity columns (Table B.52.4 for A1-D2 and B.52.10/B.52.11 for method E) are copyrighted and could not be obtained from any source that reproduces them, so they are treated as an empirical data table: the whole table is read back out of the page and checked for integrity and monotonicity, the one value a public copy of the standard does show (A1, copper, 1,5 mm2 = 13,5 A) is checked exactly, and every copper column is checked against the published two-loaded-conductor Table B.52.2 through a physically bounded ratio. The aluminium columns and the buried D1/D2 columns have no independent source at all and are recorded as flagged, not passed.

tolerance: Agreement to the last digit the page prints: |got-ref| <= 0.5*10^-d + 1e-9*|ref|, with d = 1 decimal for the design current and the corrected ampacity (A), 0 decimals for the ampacity column of the candidate table, 2 decimals for voltage drop (%) and losses (kW), 3 decimals for every correction factor, 1 decimal for the adiabatic minimum section (mm2) and the short-circuit withstand (kA). Every graded quantity is a closed form on both sides, so the only physical slack is double-precision round-off. The ampacity table itself is an empirical data table and is not graded to a numeric tolerance: it is checked for integrity, for one exact primary-source value, and against a 0.82-0.96 (0.78-0.90 for method E) ratio band to the published two-loaded-conductor table with no cell more than 0.06 from its column median.

cases.note: Every current-carrying-capacity cell the page will produce, read back through the DOM with all correction factors = 1, must be strictly increasing with cross-section within each method/material column, and every cell absent from the table must fail closed instead of returning a number.
The one Table B.52.4 value visible in a publicly readable copy of IEC 60364-5-52: method A1, copper, 1,5 mm2, three loaded conductors = 13,5 A.

Method A1, copper: the three-loaded-conductor column the page uses is checked against the published two-loaded-conductor column of IEC 60364-5-52 Table B.52.2. Three loaded conductors must carry between 4 % and 18 % less than two, and the ratio must vary smoothly with cross-section (no cell more than 0.06 from the column median). This is a consistency bound, not a value-by-value verification: it would catch a transposed row, a mistyped cell or the wrong insulation column, but it cannot confirm the last digit of a tabulated ampere value.

coverage.note: Supported cells are (material, reference method, cross-section) combinations that return a number. The page tabulates one insulation column only - PVC / 70 C conductor temperature, three loaded conductors - and eight of the ten reference methods of IEC 60364-5-52 Table B.52.1 (F and G, single-core cables in free air, are absent). XLPE is usable only when the terminals limit the conductor to 70 C, where the standard requires the 70 C column anyway; XLPE at 90 C and two loaded conductors both fail closed.

environment: Chromium (Playwright) on Linux, file:// origin, ?lang=en. Reference generated by python 3 (bench-src/ref/gen_cablesizing.py).
not_benchmarked: The aluminium current-carrying-capacity columns (IEC 60364-5-52 Table B.52.4 aluminium half and Table B.52.11) and the buried columns D1 and D2 of Table B.52.4: no accessible source reproduces those numbers, so they are NOT verified here. They are recorded verbatim under "ungraded_data" so a reader holding the standard can check them cell by cell. 160 of the 256 table cells fall in that ungraded group.

The copper columns A1, A2, B1, B2, C and E are checked only for integrity, for the single primary-source value A1/1,5 mm2 = 13,5 A, and against a ratio band to the published two-loaded-conductor Table B.52.2. That bound would catch a transposed row, a mistyped cell or the wrong insulation column; it does not confirm the last digit of a tabulated ampere value.
Reference methods F and G of IEC 60364-5-52 Table B.52.1 (single-core cables in free air, touching or spaced) are not offered by the page at all.
Cross-sections above 300 mm2, parallel conductors, harmonic-loaded neutrals, mineral-insulated cables (Tables B.52.6 to B.52.9) and depth-of-burial corrections are outside the page.

The conductor resistivity used for voltage drop and losses: the page uses 22.21 (Cu/PVC), 23.69 (Cu/XLPE), 35.29 (Al/PVC) and 37.65 (Al/XLPE) ohm mm2/km, a physical rho_20 x [1+alpha(theta-20)] model, whereas IEC 60364-5-52 Annex G prescribes rho1 = 1,25 rho_20 = 22,5 (Cu) and 36,0 (Al) ohm mm2/km. The page therefore reports a voltage drop 1.29 % (Cu) and 1.97 % (Al) lower than the Annex G convention. The drop EQUATION is graded against Annex G; the resistivity constant is a disclosed model choice, not graded.
crosscheck: Two independent transcriptions of IEC 60364-5-52 Table B.52.14 (ambient air) and of the buried-duct row of Table B.52.16 were compared - the Schneider Electric Electrical Installation Guide chapter G and ECalPro's published transcription - and agree on every value to the last digit, so the correction-factor reference is not resting on a single secondary source.
provenance_note: Every reference value is recomputed by bench-src/ref/gen_cablesizing.py from the sources this artifact cites; that generator was re-run against this tree on 2026-10-03 and its output compared with the deployed corpus leaf by leaf at 4 880 leaves, 0 differing, so no case reuses a stored ref and none carries ref_source "recorded".
